To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The structure of the complex between radixin and the full-length ICAM-2 cytoplasmic-tail peptide has been determined.
we have obtained crystals of the radixin-ICAM-2 complex and have determined the crystal structure to 2.6 A resolution.
the structure of the complex formed between the FERM domain of radixin and the cytoplasmatic tail of ICAM-2 has been solved to a resolution of about 2.6 A.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural characterization of a protein complex between the FERM domain of radixin and the cytoplasm tail of ICAM-2.

the structure of the complex between a FERM domain of radixin and the cytoplasmatic tail of intercellular molecule 2, which has been crystallized and the structure of the protein-protein complex determined by X-ray crystallography.
the structural and functional analysis of proteins involved in the regulation of the actin cytoskeleton.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FERM domain of radixin binds ICAM-2 in a way similar to that of moesin.

the FERM domain of radixin binds the cytoplasmatic tail of ICAM-2 in a manner similar to the FERM domain from ezrin, and that the binding of radixin to ICAM-2 is mediated by two different sites in the FERM domain.
the radixin FIRM domain binds to the cytoplamic tail of ICAM-2 in a manner similar to that of ezrin, which has been shown to bind ICAM-2 by a similar mode.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystallographic characterization of a radixin-ICAM-2 complex has been initiated.
we have obtained the first crystallographic data on a complex between the FERM domain of an ERM protein and the cytoplasmatic domain of an integral membrane protein.
the crystal structure of the complex between radixin FERM and the cytoplasm tail of ICAM-2 will be solved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have determined that the FERM domain of radixin is able to interact with the cytoplamsic tail of ICAM-2 in a manner that is consistent with that of ezrin, a closely related ERM protein.

the FERM domain of radixin binds to the ICAM-2 tail with a high degree of specificity and that the complex is stabilized by the formation of a hydrophobic core and a hydrogen bond between the FERM domain and ICAM-2.

the FERM domain is a modular protein domain that can bind a wide range of different cytoplasmic peptides, which is in agreement with the fact that the FERM domains of different ERM proteins are highly homologous.
